description: Franka FR3 holds press plate H by its handle above soft block A, lowers it onto the block, compresses the block to 5 % of its settled height under a closed-loop rule shared by both platforms, holds 1 s, unloads and observes recovery for 2 s.
units: m, kg, s; Z up, X towards the worktop, Y to the robot's left

platform_solvers.dexsim: DexUniSolverCfg(contact_mode='full', coupling='two_way'): MuJoCo owns the Franka; VBD owns the soft block, the press plate and static shapes; per-vertex particle-shape contact
platform_solvers.isaaclab: Newton CouplerProxy: MuJoCo-Warp entry owns the Franka; VBD entry owns the soft block, the press plate and static shapes; hand and fingers are proxied into VBD; per-vertex particle contact

robot.model_note: Newton-assets FR3 arm + Franka Hand (franka_hand_white); the repo panda_arm_hand.urdf has no local meshes.
robot.finger_mimic: both finger joints are driven independently with identical targets on both platforms
robot.gravity: robot links do not feel gravity (DexSim gravity compensation 1.0 / IsaacLab disable_gravity)

soft_block.tet_split: Freudenthal 6 tets per hexahedral cell (shared main diagonal)

press_plate.edge_fillet: not modelled (plain boxes); 3 mm fillet from the plan is a pilot deviation
notes: fingertip pads close on the 20 mm handle between a collar below and a cap above (1 mm clearance) with guide walls beside the pads along X (1 mm clearance); the plate is held by pad normal contact, not grip friction (round-1 pilot: friction-only grip slipped at 1-2 N in DexSim and dropped the plate in Isaac Lab)
the episode starts with the plate already held: fingers closed on the handle, plate hanging on the pads by its cap (plate base bottom = TCP - tcp_above_base_bottom)
the plate is a free rigid body owned by VBD on both platforms (round-1 pilot: a MuJoCo-owned plate penetrated the block in DexSim and went NaN in Isaac Lab)
part boxes, density, mass, centre of mass and inertia are derived once into inputs/s01c_plate.json

contact.friction_rule: every shape and particle set uses mu=0.6, so Newton's sqrt(mu_a*mu_b) and average blends both give 0.6
contact.shape_margin_note: explicit on both platforms: DexSim NewtonCollisionDesc defaults to margin=0.001 m, Isaac Lab NewtonShapeCfg to 0.0; round 1 left the DexSim default, so DexSim shapes were 1 mm thicker
contact.contact_model: per-vertex particle-shape contact on both platforms: DexSim contact_mode='full' (required for two-way with a VBD-owned body) leaves collision_options enable_rigid_soft_full_surface_contact at False; Isaac Lab passes enable_rigid_soft_full_surface_contact=False. Round 1 wrongly reported DexSim as full-surface

solver.vbd_iterations_note: 40 = smallest tested count at which task s00 passes every check on both platforms (2026-10-21 sweep on the task, numbers in results/S01C_DECISIONS.md: 10 -> DexSim grip slip 3.09 mm; 20 -> Isaac Lab misses the target in 3 s; 40 -> both pass, 43/54 ms per frame). Round 1 used 160 (3-4x the cost); it is not used
solver.parity_note: set explicitly on both platforms (2026-10-21): DexUni defaults to staggered coupling, Isaac Lab's CouplerProxyMappingCfg to lagged; the round-2 DexSim script set friction_epsilon=1e-4 and rigid_contact_hard=False while Isaac Lab ran Newton's defaults (0.01, True); Isaac Lab used an elliptic MuJoCo cone, DexUni the pyramidal default; DexUni proxies every MuJoCo link into VBD, Isaac Lab only the hand and fingers

trajectory.ik_table_note: TCP z offsets relative to the nominal contact TCP height; all motion is vertical at block_xy with the fixed top-down orientation
trajectory.controller: closed-loop rule implemented identically in both platform scripts (class CompressionController; tools/analyze.py checks the two class sources are identical): descend at press_speed until the 6-frame mean of h=max(z)-min(z) <= h0*(1-target); hold with dz = -gain*(h-h_target)*dt clipped to hold_max_speed; quintic unload; hold position while recovering
trajectory.height_filter_note: the controller uses a 6-frame (0.1 s) moving average of h=max(z)-min(z); pilot: the raw value jitters 1-2 % from node vibration and made the 5 % run stop late (7.8 % hold). Reported metrics use the raw per-frame h

target_note: the 10 % level of round 1 is dropped for now (user decision 2026-10-20)

initial_states.rule: s00 is nominal; s01-s09 move the soft block in the table plane by dx, dy ~ U(-3, 3) mm and yaw ~ U(-3, 3) deg about its vertical axis; the robot, plate and joint targets are unchanged, so the plate meets the block off-centre. Bounds keep the rotated block footprint inside the 70 mm plate (worst corner 34.5 mm < 35 mm). The file stores the actual world-space node positions of every state.

variants_note: plan 3.3 (5/10/20 substep convergence) and 7.2 (CUDA Graph vs direct paired check); each variant is run on state s00; nominal = 10 substeps with CUDA Graph

bench.description: robot-free material bench (plan 3.3): a flat rigid weight of bench_mass (weight_size, uniform density, low centre of mass) is released bench_gap above the block while the robot stays parked away from it; the static compression over measure_window is compared with a linear-elastic estimate
bench.estimate: uniaxial, frictionless ends: dh = H*(m*g/A + rho*g*H/2)/E
bench.weight_note: pilot 2026-10-21: the handled press plate (COM ~14 mm above its base) loaded to 0.5 kg rocked on the block on both platforms (DexSim: slid off at 160 iterations; Isaac Lab: settled with ~5 deg tilt), so the bench uses a flat weight, see results/S01C_DECISIONS.md
bench.status: informational, not a gate: with a free 0.5 kg rigid weight on the 0.07 g nodes neither platform converges to the linear-elastic estimate at practical iteration counts (10-40 iterations: 0.1-0.6 mm vs 2.87 mm; higher counts or contact ke 2e3-2e4, 40 substeps, no damping or a 4-cell mesh did not fix it, and 40+ iterations sometimes flip the weight). The block's effective stiffness is therefore not verified; S01-C reports geometric response only. Sweep numbers: results/S01C_DECISIONS.md

measurement.phase_windows: hold metrics use the last 0.8 s of the hold phase; recovery is read 2.0 s after the unload phase ends; all phase boundaries are recorded per frame

outputs: depth (planar distance to the image plane, m)
images.full: every 30 Hz frame: RGB video + depth/segmentation arrays (state s00 runs)
images.keyframes: RGB video every 30 Hz frame; depth/segmentation at phase starts, hold end and episode end (perturbed states and variants), to bound data volume

measurement.cameras_note: the plan asks for top + oblique views; a vertical top view (eye 0.48,-0.10,1.35) only shows the Franka hand, which covers the block during the whole episode (2026-10-21 check), so the second camera looks down at 45 deg from +X, past the 5 cm-thick side of the hand
measurement.depth_background: no-hit pixels: DexSim returns a very large value (~1e16), Isaac Lab returns 0 (depth_clipping_behavior='none'); raw values are stored, plots mask both
measurement.resolution_note: cameras render at camera_resolution (1280x960) for the HD comparison video; depth, segmentation and RGB keyframes are stored at the plan's 640x480 by taking every image_downsample-th pixel (row/column 0, 2, 4, ...), with the matching intrinsics K stored next to them; the full-resolution K is in the run manifest
measurement.video_policy: only one exported video per task: tools/analyze.py writes videos/s01c_comparison.mp4 (2x2: columns platform, rows oblique/front45, HD, real-time frame-rate overlay). The s00 full runs keep rgb_<camera>.mp4 inside their raw_data run directory as the source; other runs keep RGB only as keyframes in images_<camera>.npz
